cases.label: canonical value
cases.rationale: the shortest spelling that satisfies all four canonical rules; a decoder that refuses a length of 2 modulo 4, or that answers uppercase hex, answers wrongly here.

cases.label: padded spelling
cases.rationale: the same octets with padding; every mainstream decoder accepts this spelling, and the strict field rule refuses it.

cases.label: trailing bits set
cases.rationale: unused trailing bits set; no runtime decoder enforces this rule by itself, so a bridge that decodes without re-encoding and comparing answers the same octets as the first case.

cases.label: standard-alphabet spelling
cases.rationale: the standard base64 alphabet in place of the url alphabet; a bridge that routes the value through a permissive decoder accepting both alphabets answers the octets.

cases.label: known answer
cases.rationale: a 16-octet key selects AES-128-GCM, and the tag follows the ciphertext in one buffer; a bridge that reads the tag off the front of the buffer, or that hands the whole buffer to a runtime taking the tag separately, refuses a carrier that opens.

cases.label: carrier under other additional data
cases.rationale: the carrier of the first case under other additional data; a bridge that drops the aad member, or that reports a tag failure as a nonzero exit, answers wrongly here.

cases.label: a Root for the premium fifteen-minute family
cases.rationale: 32-octet ikm and a 41-octet info carrying 0x00 and octets above 0x7f; an implementation that routes info through a text string answers other bytes, and one that returns the whole 32-octet block instead of 16 octets fails here

cases.label: a Root for a longer access-group and five-minute geometry
cases.rationale: a 45-octet info, longer than every other row; an implementation that reads info out of a fixed-width buffer or truncates it to 41 octets answers other bytes

cases.label: a Root at a different window and one-chain geometry
cases.rationale: the same octet widths as the first row over other octets; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a Root under a distinct secret
cases.rationale: the first row's info octets with different key material; an implementation that passes ikm as the salt, or derives from info alone, answers the two rows alike

cases.label: one Step into position zero
cases.rationale: 16-octet ikm, half the width the four rows above supply; an implementation that accepts one fixed key width, or pads a short ikm to 32 octets, answers other bytes

cases.label: one Step whose supplied state is position ten
cases.rationale: a second row at the 16-octet ikm width; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: one Step from the terminal state
cases.rationale: a third row at the 16-octet ikm width, its ikm the first row's output; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a Leaf at position zero
cases.rationale: the info of the fifth row under one other leading octet, at the same widths; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a Leaf at an interior fifteen-minute position
cases.rationale: a 41-octet info and a 16-octet ikm once more; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a Leaf at a five-minute terminal position
cases.rationale: a second 45-octet info, the width the second row already covers; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a Leaf at a 288-position terminal
cases.rationale: the one-chain geometry's 41-octet info at the widths above; it adds no byte-level distinction and stays as a recorded known answer of the construction

cases.label: a 32-octet derivation over ASCII info
cases.rationale: the only row asking for a full 32-octet block, over a 32-octet ikm and 26 octets of ASCII info; an implementation that truncates the output to one 16-octet half, or that reads info as a text string of another encoding, answers other octets. Its output is the key that opens the wrapped carrier in aes-gcm-256/04.

cases.label: seal under additional data
cases.rationale: a 32-octet key selects AES-256-GCM, and the answer carries the 16-octet tag appended to the ciphertext; a bridge on a runtime whose API returns the tag separately and does not append it answers 16 octets of the expected value.

cases.label: seal without additional data
cases.rationale: the same seal over additional data of zero octets; a runtime whose API tells an absent aad apart from an empty one answers a different tag when a bridge passes the wrong form.

cases.label: open under additional data
cases.rationale: the carrier of the first case read back; a bridge that selects the cipher by a fixed width rather than by the key it was handed opens nothing at 32 octets.

cases.label: open without additional data
cases.rationale: the second seal read back; a bridge that refuses to pass additional data of zero octets, or that substitutes some other octets for an empty aad member, refuses a carrier that opens.

cases.label: carrier sealed under additional data, opened without it
cases.rationale: the third case with its additional data taken away; a bridge that ignores the aad member answers the plaintext here, and one that treats an empty member as a request it cannot serve exits instead of answering.

cases.label: agreement from one side
cases.rationale: the agreed x-coordinate at the full field width and no KDF over it; a bridge that hashes the secret, or that answers the whole 65-octet point, answers other octets. The secret opens the recorded carrier in aes-gcm-256/03.

cases.label: agreement from the other side
cases.rationale: the same agreement with the two halves swapped; a bridge that reads the private scalar out of the peer point, or that swaps the two inputs, holds the first case and fails this one.

cases.label: point from a recorded key
cases.rationale: the uncompressed SEC 1 encoding: the octet 0x04 and two 32-octet coordinates; a bridge that answers a compressed point, or that leaves the leading octet off, answers a different length. These are the 65 octets that lead the recorded sealed carrier.

cases.label: recorded ciphertext over a 64-octet plaintext
cases.rationale: OAEP over SHA-256 with MGF1 on the same hash and no label; a bridge on a runtime defaulting MGF1 to SHA-1, or one passing a label, refuses a ciphertext that opens. The published bound-carrier vectors record this same ciphertext, so it is carried once.

cases.label: recorded ciphertext over a 16-octet plaintext
cases.rationale: a recorded known answer of the class the first case already covers, at the same 2048-bit modulus width over a shorter plaintext.
